title: Extension of natural bilinear operations from the affine basis
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme and $M,N,P$ sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For every affine open $V$ suppose that $\beta_V:M(V)\times N(V)\to P(V)$ is $\mathcal O_X(V)$-bilinear, and suppose these maps commute with restriction between affine opens. There exist $\mathcal O_X(U)$-bilinear maps $\mu_U:M(U)\times N(U)\to P(U)$ for all opens $U$, commuting with every restriction and agreeing with $\beta_V$ on each affine open $V$. No quasi-coherence or separation hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Sheaves on Spaces, Definition 6.9.1 (0072), equalizer/sheaf axiom; applied to the affine-basis gluing step of the associated graded construction implicit in Cohomology of Schemes Lemma 087Z.

proof.text: For U and sections a,b, form beta_V(a|V,b|V) on all affine opens V contained in U. On an intersection of two such opens compare their restrictions on every affine open W in that intersection. Naturality of beta and composition of restriction maps identify both with beta_W(a|W,b|W). Sheaf separatedness on the affine basis proves equality on the whole intersection. The sheaf gluing axiom then gives a section on U with exactly these affine restrictions.

Choose these uniquely characterized glued sections as g(U,a,b). Compare g(U,a,b+b′) with g(U,a,b)+g(U,a,b′) on the affine basis; affine bilinearity proves equality. Do the same for addition in the first variable and scalar multiplication in either variable, using semilinearity of module restrictions. Package the resulting identities as curried linear maps mu_U.

For V contained in U compare the restriction of g(U,a,b) with g(V,a|V,b|V) on each affine W contained in V. Both have affine restriction beta_W(a|W,b|W), hence are equal. Taking U affine and its identity inclusion proves agreement with beta_U. The empty cover handles empty opens. No assumption that intersections of affine opens are affine is used.

lean.statement:
theorem affineBilinear_extension {X : Scheme.{u}} (M N P : X.Modules)
    (beta : ∀ V : X.affineOpens,
      M.val.obj (op V.1) →ₗ[Γ(X, V.1)] N.val.obj (op V.1) →ₗ[Γ(X, V.1)]
        P.val.obj (op V.1))
    (hbeta : ∀ (V W : X.affineOpens) (h : W.1 ≤ V.1)
      (a : M.val.obj (op V.1)) (b : N.val.obj (op V.1)),
      P.val.map (homOfLE h).op (beta V a b) =
        beta W (M.val.map (homOfLE h).op a) (N.val.map (homOfLE h).op b)) :
    ∃ mu : ∀ U : X.Opens,
      M.val.obj (op U) →ₗ[Γ(X, U)] N.val.obj (op U) →ₗ[Γ(X, U)] P.val.obj (op U),
      (∀ (U V : X.Opens) (h : V ≤ U)
        (a : M.val.obj (op U)) (b : N.val.obj (op U)),
        P.val.map (homOfLE h).op (mu U a b) =
          mu V (M.val.map (homOfLE h).op a) (N.val.map (homOfLE h).op b)) ∧
      (∀ (V : X.affineOpens) (a : M.val.obj (op V.1)) (b : N.val.obj (op V.1)),
        mu V.1 a b = beta V a b)
